title: Counter-Selector Wave 37: bounded live operational handoff
purpose: Adjudicate the first public same-object live runtime transition in which operational state is transferred into a successor process image and the same workload demonstrably continues, while preserving the distinction between bounded live continuity, portable package custody, recipient inventory acknowledgment, external review, and person-level operator evidence.

complete_bounded_live_handoff_requires: one attributable live object crosses one declared transition boundary
the outgoing runtime serializes the state needed by the incoming runtime
the incoming runtime resumes the same bounded object rather than creating an unrelated replacement
post-transition operation is observed from the transferred state
failure paths preserve or terminate the bounded object without silent partial success
the result remains explicitly scoped to the state categories and operating conditions actually observed
complete_portable_package_handoff_requir: one versioned digest-bound package identifies every transferred entry
the recipient acknowledges the exact package inventory
authority credentials dependencies open decisions and rollback state travel with that package
an independent verifier can reproduce the package-to-operation chain outside the originating runtime

components.live_object_identity: the same running sandbox workload and its envd parent cross a same-PID process-image replacement
components.state_package_identity: tmpfs handover state at /run/e2b/envd-handover.json plus the fixed successor binary path; no one portable digest-bound package joins both
components.integrity_and_version_binding: authenticated delivery, fixed executable target, strictly-newer live-version gate, and post-upgrade running-version confirmation; no exact package manifest or binary digest receipt
components.outgoing_and_incoming_runtime_identity: outgoing envd and incoming --resume-handover envd are attributable process roles across syscall.Exec
components.authority_and_credential_control: token-authenticated upgrade endpoint, fixed-path execution, LaunchDarkly or environment target gate, minimum-version gate, and pre-init fail-closed authorization
components.dependency_and_access_state: process configuration, stdio and PTY descriptors, retained terminal events, filesystem watchers, remaining timeouts, mounts, and port-forward state are carried or reconstituted
components.open_decision_and_deadline_state: remaining process timeouts and target-version decisions are carried; no general itemized open-decision and operational-dependency inventory is acknowledged
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: pre-exec failure retains the old envd and thaws safely; unrecoverable confirmed post-exec failure fails and tears down the resume; no rollback to the prior process image exists after successful exec
components.recipient_or_successor_state_acknowledgm: incoming re-adoption, handover result, live-version response, and success metrics acknowledge operational resumption; no recipient signs or acknowledges an itemized package inventory
components.successor_operation_from_transferred_sta: the same workload PID continues writing across 0.6.11 to 0.6.12 and a later 0.6.12 to 0.6.13 chain, with output growth and recovered exit state
components.independent_verification: unit, integration, dev-cluster, metrics, and multi-reviewer checks exist inside the originating project; no independent external institution reproduced the transition

positive_findings: The outgoing process serializes live state and performs a same-PID exec rather than restarting around an untracked workload.
The incoming process re-adopts the same workload descriptors, timeouts, watchers, and retained terminal state before normal operation resumes.
A live counter workload kept the same PID and advanced from seven to twenty lines across the binary replacement.
A two-hop 0.6.11 to 0.6.12 to 0.6.13 transition preserved the same workload PID across both handoffs.
Running-version confirmation prevents a transport error from being represented as a successful upgrade.
Failure handling distinguishes recoverable pre-exec failure from unrecoverable post-exec failure and prevents silent partial success.
known_limits: The streamed binary and handover state are not joined by one versioned exact-entry package manifest and digest.
The incoming runtime does not acknowledge an itemized package inventory, credentials, dependencies, and open decisions.
The end-to-end receipt is from a dev cluster and does not establish universal production assurance.
Same-system unit, integration, metrics, and review evidence are not an external independent review.
The transition proves bounded user-workload continuity, not complete custody of every possible system process.
A retained edge remains for unfrozen internal _system processes that can exit during the snapshot and degrade to a wait4 error.
A successful same-PID runtime handoff is a system-control result, not a person-to-person custody receipt.

components.live_object_identity: a responsibility-transfer proof object is identified; a live operational workload is not
components.state_package_identity: the portable proof binds transfer, audit, Bundle, Policy, certificate, and signatures into one proof structure
components.integrity_and_version_binding: cryptographic roots, signatures, trusted timestamp, and certificate are recalculated and substitution-tested
components.outgoing_and_incoming_runtime_identity: outgoing and incoming Participants are explicit signers, but no outgoing and incoming runtime execution roles are observed
components.authority_and_credential_control: trusted key identity, validity, revocation, signing time, and participant-role identity are checked
components.dependency_and_access_state: proof dependencies are bound; operational runtime dependencies and access state are outside the object
components.open_decision_and_deadline_state: the Policy decision is independently replayed; live operational open decisions and deadlines are absent
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: modified Bundle, audit lineage, Participant signatures, and invalid trust state fail closed
components.recipient_or_successor_state_acknowledgm: the incoming Participant signs the proof root, not an itemized operational package inventory
components.successor_operation_from_transferred_sta: not observed and physical actuation remains outside PDS scope
components.independent_verification: the same system independently recalculates the full portable proof; no external institution reproduces live operation

positive_findings: Every proof component is bound to one deterministic root.
Outgoing and incoming Participants sign the same proof.
The complete portable proof is recalculated from its supplied artifacts.
Audit-lineage, Bundle-manifest, and incoming-signature substitution fail closed.
known_limits: The proof object is not an operational runtime-state package.
The incoming signature is not an itemized inventory receipt for runtime dependencies and credentials.
No successor operates a live object from the proof.
Physical actuation is explicitly outside scope.
Same-project independent recalculation is not an external independent review.
A complete proof chain does not establish person-level operator capacity.

components.live_object_identity: one FAT project and workbook identity is intended to persist across workspaces; no independently observed live recipient is bound
components.state_package_identity: versioned ARSAS package with manifest, snapshot, workbook, evidence journals, reports, and README
components.integrity_and_version_binding: manifest hashes, evidence hash chains, modern report hashes, and tamper tests exist, subject to unresolved compatibility and validation defects
components.outgoing_and_incoming_runtime_identity: exporter and importer software roles exist; no named outgoing and incoming operational participants are bound
components.authority_and_credential_control: active IED sessions block export; a complete credential, environment, and authority ledger is absent
components.dependency_and_access_state: workbook, snapshot, reports, and evidence are represented; environment dependencies and total archive expansion are incomplete
components.open_decision_and_deadline_state: completed and remaining test scope is persisted; no package-level decision and deadline receipt is acknowledged
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_failure_contai: atomic writes, tamper rejection, collision preservation, and continuity downgrade exist; stale overwrite and archive-budget defects remain
components.recipient_or_successor_state_acknowledgm: automated import and regression success exist; no named recipient acknowledges one exact inventory
components.successor_operation_from_transferred_sta: automated cross-workspace restoration is tested; independently observed field continuation is absent
components.independent_verification: two automated review surfaces preserve seven defects and do not clear the package

positive_findings: A versioned portable package exists and is executed in cross-workspace regression.
Snapshot, workbook, report, and evidence integrity surfaces are present.
Tampered content is rejected in bounded tests.
Lost live continuity is downgraded instead of silently preserved.
known_limits: Evidence journals can mix across workbook hashes sharing a ProjectId.
An older package can overwrite newer local progress.
Archive limits do not create an aggregate decompression budget.
Null required manifest members can escape the intended failure path.
Modern packages can omit native-report hashes through legacy compatibility.
Non-ASCII evidence text can be lost in the PDF.
Per-IED headers can omit failed-point counts.

next_action: Seek one real same-object transition that joins E2B-grade live successor operation with a versioned digest-bound portable package, an itemized recipient inventory acknowledgment, complete authority and dependency state, and genuinely external review. Do not assemble those components from different systems or convert a system control into person support.
